notes: This source/test traceability contract covers Umbra's bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 Unsubscribe Object Class Directed Interactions service in its opt-in, non-installable development profile. The focused production-filesystem regression rejects undefined object and interaction class designators without appending a successful-void report. It then verifies the official C++ interaction-set overload emits ObjectClassHandle type 36 plus the supplied Optional set of directed interaction designators as InteractionClassHandleSet type 28; an explicitly supplied empty set remains type-28 []; and the official whole-class overload retains that required optional slot as type-34 Null. Report appends occur only after the registry accepts the unsubscription. The page-102 §5.13 candidates retain their correct service owner, but the page-103 continuation carrying the no-subsequent-receive postcondition is incorrectly owned by §5.14.3; RL-080 records that cross-page ownership defect. Table 5's rotated InteractionClassHandleSet row has no row-level Requirements Lab candidate (RL-067/RL-076). Complete directed unsubscription/delivery matrices, MOM interaction delivery, timestamped behavior, DDM, remote transport, packaging, validation, and conformance remain outside this slice.
